entries.subject: Time an explicit seek from the physical read head during a read

lines: * physical head while paused or in standby. Both use the source tape.
* The source measures a seek from CurSector, its physical read head. An
* established read keeps that head CDC_SECTOR_PIPE_COUNT (2) sectors
* ahead of the sector handed to the guest, because HandlePlayRead fills

entries.subject: cdrom: report the cycling paused-drive sub-Q from GetlocP

lines: /* Source SubQBuf_Safe latch — the sector whose sub-Q the drive last decoded.
* HandlePlayRead reads the sector AT CurSector and decodes its Q before
* advancing the cursor, so the decoded position is the pre-increment value,
* one behind the physical head tracked above. The source keeps calling
* HandlePlayRead while the drive is paused or in standby, so this latch goes
* on cycling after a Pause; it only freezes when the drive seeks or stops,
* which is exactly when source_drive_head_valid is cleared. -1 = never
/* Stopped Nymashock drive. GetlocP returns SubQBuf_Safe, and the
* source keeps decoding sub-Q while paused: HandlePlayRead runs
* for DS_PAUSED and DS_STANDBY too, and its tail cycles the head
* so a paused drive walks a nine-sector window below the position
* Pause stopped at. Reporting the last sector handed to the guest
* instead is right only for the first tick after the Pause. */

entries.note: GetlocP returns SubQBuf_Safe, and the source keeps decoding sub-Q while the drive is stopped: Update() calls HandlePlayRead for DS_PAUSED and DS_STANDBY, whose tail runs CurSector++ then, while stopped, retreats nine whenever CurSector reaches SeekTarget+2. A paused drive therefore walks a nine-sector window, one decode per sector period. Reporting the last sector handed to the guest is correct only for the first tick after a Pause. Mega Man X5 returns 7311-7466 were the single GetlocP issued five frames after a Pause: source 185243, ours 185251, and twelve completed sector periods of the cycle from 185250 land on 185243 exactly. Scoped to a stopped Nymashock drive; the reading branch already matched and Octoshock titles never reach it.

entries.subject: sio: answer DualShock 0x45 the way the source does

lines: /* 0x45 "Query Model and Mode". The source builds this reply in two
* That source index is the SECOND byte of the 0x4501 phase, i.e. the
* fifth byte of the whole reply, after 0xF3 0x5A <type> 0x02 — not
* pad_response[3], which is the constant 0x02. Writing it there
* destroyed the constant and left a hard-coded analog-on in the real
* mode slot, so we answered 03 00 01 where the source answers

entries.note: Mega Man X5 return 1090 diverged by three bytes with an identical clock; the game queues SIO bytes verbatim, so the diverging RAM record was the reply. frontio.c builds 0x45 as 01 02 <analog_mode> 02 01 00. Two faults: device type 0x03 instead of 0x01, and the live-mode override writing pad_response[3] (the constant 0x02) instead of [4], destroying the constant and hard-coding analog-on in the mode slot. The pinned 260-transaction Nymashock fixture issues no 0x45, which is why this survived.

entries.subject: sio: select the 0x46/0x47/0x4C replies from their data byte

lines: /* 0x46/0x47/0x4C do not have one fixed reply: the source selects it from
* the data byte at position 3, which arrives paired with response index 2
* (frontio.c cases 0x4601, 0x4701, 0x4C01). The canned tables above are
* only the data == 0x00 variant, so a game that asks with 0x01 got the
* wrong answer — Mega Man X5 issues 0x4C with 0x01 and the source replies
* Reply bytes 3..7 are the five phase-1 bytes; byte 2 is the phase-0 byte
/* 0x47 has no 0x01 case: anything other than 0x00 replies zeros. */

entries.note: With 0x45 fixed the divergence moved to return 1098, where Mega Man X5 issues 0x4C with data 0x01. The source selects these replies from the data byte; our canned tables held only the data==0x00 variant. 0x46: 00 -> 00 01 02 00 0A, 01 -> 00 01 01 01 14, else zeros. 0x47: 00 -> 00 02 00 01 00, else zeros. 0x4C: 00 -> 00 00 04 00 00, 01 -> 00 00 07 00 00, else zeros. The pinned 260-transaction Nymashock fixture issues none of 0x46/0x47/0x4C.

/* INCMD_PLINE: a poly-line consumes further vertices after its opening packet until a
* terminator word. pline_command is the source's InCmd_CC; pline_color/pline_vertex are

* two-vertex packet the cost model and renderer already take. */
/* Commands_40_5F: the source gives every entry in 0x40-0x5F the same LINE_HELPER, so the whole
* family is one shape. Bit 3 selects a poly-line and bit 4 gouraud shading; bit 3 changes only
* the FIFO bookkeeping, never the rasterisation, because DrawLine is templated on <goraud,
/* INCMD_PLINE consumes 1 + goraud words per continuation segment: a vertex, preceded by a
/* ProcessFIFO tests the terminator before it tests the segment length, so it needs one word. */
/* CalcFIFOReadyBit clears the bit for INCMD_PLINE exactly as it does for INCMD_QUAD. */
/* INCMD_PLINE. The terminator is tested before the segment length and consumes one
* word. A segment is projected as the ordinary two-vertex packet it draws as, with
* InPLine_PrevPoint supplying point 0, so the cost model, the dispatch block's start
* coordinate and the renderer all take it unchanged. The main FIFO tail's -2 is never
* reached from this branch, so a segment is charged the draw cost alone. */
/* Command_DrawLine keeps points[1] as InPLine_PrevPoint; a flat line's second
* point carries the first point's colour. */
/* The whole line family, 0x40-0x5F. A poly-line segment reaches here as the ordinary
* two-vertex packet it draws as: DrawLine is templated on <goraud, BlendMode,
* MaskEval_TA>, so the poly-line bit never reaches rasterisation. */
